title: "pokemon but with the johnson solids", then polyhedra folded up from flat nets
summary: On Sun 15 Nov 04:59Z @oscillatory.net (274 followers) posted a picture of all 92 Johnson solids with the words: intrusive thought when i look at this "pokemon but with the johnson solids" (38 likes), and in a reply a worked example that begins "triangular cupola, i choose you!" and admits "i've never actually played pokemon". On Mon 16 Nov 15:42Z the first account posted a video of a tool for building polyhedral nets and folding them up, with a "magnetic assist" that snaps close edges together. @minormobius.bsky.social (7,162 followers) replied "Ooh I had NOT thought about oragami polychora for understanding the 4d thank you for that push. Fabulous work on all fronts", and a little over two hours later posted a page of nets that fold into four-dimensional shapes. Later posts by @oscillatory.net: a video of a square antiprism folded from a net ("this is pretty satisfying"); the bilunabirotunda (J91) rebuilt as net and solid, in a post that calls @minormobius.bsky.social's Johnson solid website "by far the most convenient way i've found for quickly looking up the 3d shapes"; a screenshot of a new git branch named 'hebesphenomegacorona' captioned "the heart wants what it wants (18 equilateral triangle faces on a convex polyhedron)"; and on Thu 19 Nov 02:34Z a video captioned "at last, i have created the hebesphenomegacorona triforce bowtie".

posts.alt:
Example battle
You control a triangular cupola.

Its bottom face is currently a hexagon. You want to activate a special ability associated with its top triangle.

You can't access that triangle directly. You have to tip through intermediate faces.

Meanwhile, your opponent controls an elongated square pyramid and is maneuvering toward a powerful pentagonal attack.

The gameplay becomes a mixture of:
- Pokémon's ability selection and team composition.
- A tactical board game with spatial positioning.
- A puzzle about navigating the surface of a polyhedron.
The important difference from conventional Pokémon is that your ability selection is constrained by your creature's current orientation.
